---
title: Radicle
description: "Read Radicle repositories, issues, patches, reviews, files and commits from a seed node, without credentials."
icon: i-custom-radicle
---

[Radicle](https://radicle.dev) is a peer-to-peer forge built on Git. There's no central server. Repositories, issues and patches travel between nodes. The provider reads repositories, issues, patches, reviews, files, branches, tags and commits from one seed node's HTTP API.

::note
This provider is experimental. Radicle's HTTP API still changes between httpd releases. See [Capabilities](/concepts/capabilities) for what the provider supports.
::

## Authentication

The provider uses `https://seed.radicle.dev` by default and appends `/api/v1`. Want another node? Set `baseUrl` to a node running radicle-httpd, such as `https://iris.radicle.xyz`. Refs use that node's host as their `instance`.

The API needs no credentials, and the provider takes none. Leave `auth` out or use `{ type: 'anonymous' }`. No token to create, no scopes to guess. A node serves only public repositories.

The provider only reads. It can't create issues, comment, review or merge. Radicle writes are signed by your key on your own node. An HTTP API can't do that.

## Repositories

A Radicle repository has delegates, not an owner. The provider puts `'rad'` in the owner field, giving nobody a rather short name. The repository id is the honest address. A name anyone can pick isn't an address.

Use the globally unique RID without its `rad:` prefix as `name`. The prefix works too. `externalId` holds the full RID. `repo.displayName` comes from the identity document, such as `radicle-job`.

```ts
import { radicle } from 'forges/radicle'

const forge = radicle()
const repo = await forge.repos.get({
  forge: 'radicle',
  instance: forge.instance,
  owner: 'rad',
  name: 'z2UcCU1LgMshWvXj6hXSDDrwB8q8M',
})
```

An account is a DID, such as `did:key:z6Mk...`. The actor's `login` and `id` are the DID. Its name is the node's alias, when available. `repos.byOwner()` lists repositories maintained by a delegate. Pass its DID as the namespace owner. Anything else rejects with `UnsupportedOperationError`.

## Issues and patches

Issue and patch ids are Git object ids, with 40 hex characters. Put the id in a thread ref's `number`. Patches are pull requests in the data model. An issue's description is its first comment, so `threads.comments()` starts with the first reply. An issue closed as solved has `stateReason` `'completed'`.

Open and draft patches both have state `'open'`. Drafts also set `isDraft`. Archived patches are `'closed'`, and merged patches are `'merged'`. With state `'open'`, `threads.list()` returns open patches first, then drafts. httpd keeps drafts apart. State `'closed'` lists archived patches.

Patches have revisions. `threads.files()` and `threads.commits()` read the latest revision against its original base. `threads.reviews()` lists reviews across every revision. Accept maps to `'approved'`, and reject maps to `'changes_requested'`.

## Revisions and refs

httpd only accepts full commit SHAs. The provider resolves branches, tags and `HEAD` through the canonical refs agreed on by delegates. `contents.branches()` and `contents.tags()` list those refs. A name outside them rejects with `NotFoundError`.

httpd reports no totals. The cursor is a page number, and a listing ends at the first short page. Each page holds at most 100 items.

## Web URLs

Links point to the Radicle explorer at `https://radicle.network/nodes/<host>/<rid>`. `parseUrl()` reads them back, including links to issues, patches, commits and files. An explorer link for another node is a different instance. It doesn't parse.
